upstream.label: is interrupted when scope is closed

cases.behavior: Closing an owning scope interrupts its child and waits for child cleanup before parent cleanup.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: The Ergo fixture asserts completed child-before-parent release, not upstream Scope internals or the entire forkScoped API.

upstream.label: scoped combines usage and finalizer failures

cases.behavior: An expected failure and a cleanup defect both survive scope closure.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Ergo uses Timeout plus an acquired-resource cleanup defect, including attempted Timeout recovery. This is a behavior comparison, not a port of generic addFinalizer syntax.

upstream.label: sleep - does not require passage of wall time

cases.behavior: Advancing test program time admits an already-forked sleeper and allows its join without waiting for the requested wall-clock delay.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Ergo tests explicit TestClock/TestScheduler providers and an admitted but unstarted fork at 36000000 milliseconds (10 hours), under a 15-second watchdog per target; they do not assert all TestClock adjustment/precision behavior.

cases.behavior: A deadline reports a typed timeout; a timer defect must retain its Cause rather than being recast as that timeout.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Upstream asserts Cause.TimeoutError with a duration message. Ergo declares nominal Timeout and an explicit Scheduler capability; its supplemental invalid-duration timer test also checks cleanup defects. This does not claim identical timeout APIs or full upstream case parity.

upstream.label: interrupting a build does not hang current or later requesters

cases.behavior: Interrupting one requester of a shared layer acquisition leaves other current and later requesters able to complete.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Upstream MemoMap builds in the first requester's fiber, so interrupting it completes the shared entry with that interruption for every waiter. Ergo producers belong to the provision build: cancelling one waiter abandons only its own wait, the producer continues, and every other waiter observes the actual shared outcome. Whole-build cancellation is the only static-surface trigger; the evidence drives the emitted Go runtime seam directly until a language caller exists.

upstream.label: layers can be acquired in parallel

cases.behavior: Independent selected nodes acquire concurrently; cancelling the build while one producer never completes still returns after every producer joins.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Ergo asserts the cancelDuringConcurrentAcquisition trace: a cooperative producer observes cancellation, a masked concurrent acquisition completes late, nothing is released or returned before both join, and the cause is the caller's interruption alone. It drives the emitted Go runtime seam directly, not upstream Layer.merge.

upstream.label: preserves a failure when a shared layer build is interrupted

cases.behavior: When a sibling fails while a shared node is still being acquired and another node waits on it, the build fails with the actual failure; the abort-induced interruption of the shared node does not replace or fabricate it.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Ergo asserts the partialFailureRollback trace: the pending shared producer is cancelled and joined, its waiter never constructs, rollback releases dependents first and the typed failure stays primary beside every cleanup defect. Only the fail case is exercised; defect primary selection is covered by the Go runtime suite.

cases.behavior: Interrupting a build releases every resource that some node acquired, including one whose uninterruptible acquisition completes after the interruption.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Upstream only checks that acquired implies released after an arbitrary interruption point. Ergo fixes the interruption point while two producers run and asserts the exact release order and that the late acquisition is released exactly once.

upstream.label: finalizers with multiple layers with provideTo

cases.behavior: Node finalizers run after the provided program's, dependents before their dependencies.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Ergo asserts the programFailureWithCleanupDefects trace, which also requires every finalizer to run after a program failure and each cleanup defect to follow the program failure in close order. Independent nodes close sequentially in reverse canonical order; concurrent closure is permitted but not exercised.

cases.behavior: Separate provisions are separate builds with independent acquisition tables: a node is acquired again by each build, a failed build retains its one outcome and is retried only by a new explicit build, and a caller-owned borrowed resource stays open across both.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Upstream shares one MemoMap across builds so the second build reuses the first build's layer. Ergo has no shared or global memo map; explicit cross-build leases remain libraries with their own owning scope.
